acceptanceCriteria.statement: The nav computer I open with N is drawn at the game's resolution, not the window's — it lands on the same pixel grid as the world behind it instead of sitting on top of it sharp. All three of the resolutions I kept work.

verifyVia.input: Press N with Resolution at 240p, then change it to 288 and 360 with the nav open.
verifyVia.observable: The overlay canvas backing store equals resolveRenderBuffer(innerWidth, innerHeight) — 427x240, 512x288, 640x360 on a 1600x900 viewport — while its CSS box stays the full panel, and #nav-computer-canvas carries image-rendering: pixelated so it upscales. Today NavComputer._resizeCanvas (src/ui/NavComputer.js:612-617) sets canvas.width = rect.width off getBoundingClientRect(), giving ~1560x860: 3.58x the world's line count. ⭐ THE IDIOM ALREADY EXISTS TWICE — SupercruiseHud._syncBuffer (SupercruiseHud.js:114-129) and TargetingReticle._resize (TargetingReticle.js:213-226) both set the backing store from resolveRenderBuffer and the style box from the window, with the pixelated pair in style.css:38-40. _resizeCanvas becomes that shape. NavComputer imports nothing from renderBuffer today.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Everything I could click before, I can still click. The tabs, a sector tile, a star, a body and the WARP/BURN button all respond where they look.

verifyVia.input: At 240p, click each of the five level tabs, a 2D tile, a prism star, a body in SYSTEM, and the commit button.
verifyVia.observable: Level changes on each tab, the tile drills, the star and body select, and the commit button fires the burn/warp. ⭐ THE MAPPING SHOULD ALREADY BE CORRECT AND THAT IS WHY THIS AC EXISTS RATHER THAN A BUILD STEP: _getCanvasPos (NavComputer.js:4334-4339) maps (e.clientX - rect.left) * (canvas.width / rect.width), and every draw site in the file works in backing-store units too, so shrinking the store to 427 changes the ratio from 1.0 to 0.274 on BOTH sides and cancels. A click at the CSS centre (780,430) of a 1560x860 box lands at (213.5,120) — the centre of a 427x240 buffer. This is an unverified prediction until it is driven live; the eight hit-test sites are :4060, :4364, :4378-4380 and :4440-4443.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The nav I have today is still there as the thing to compare against — I flip to it and it is exactly what I already had, so the comparison is against the real product and not against a fourth thing nobody designed.

verifyVia.input: Open the nav with no view mode selected, at every buffer, and compare the emitted pixels against the pre-change build.
verifyVia.observable: Byte-identical. viewMode defaults to null and null is today's path by construction — render() returns before any mode code, exactly the way pixelType: null never enters navPixelType.js. ⭐ AND THIS IS WHY navLayout's SATURATION IS NOT BEING TOUCHED, against the predecessor handoff's §4.7 which called it 'the single biggest thing to fix': that finding assumed the 240p fullscreen nav would be BUILT ON the existing renderer, so its desktop chrome (tabH 32 = 13.3% of 240 rows, navMapSize 160 = a 25% square in a 427-wide frame) would be inherited. Max instead ruled on two designs that draw their OWN chrome and never call navTabHeight / navChromeReserve / navMapSize. Nothing production-side is left above the h >= 160 threshold once the modes own the low-res surface, so desaturating would move the shipped overlay and the pinned fixtures to fix a surface that no longer exists. §4.7 reopens the moment anything asks the LEGACY renderer to draw into a low-res buffer.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The nav panel on the cockpit glass that I already passed is exactly as it was.

verifyVia.input: Render the cockpit NAV panel headlessly at 52x43 before and after the change and compare.
verifyVia.observable: The panel instance's emitted pixels are unchanged and the src/cockpit suite is still 698 green. The panel and the overlay are TWO SEPARATE NavComputer instances (main.js:4700 builds the cockpit's, main.js:5895 builds _domNavComputer), so the view-mode axis is written on the DOM instance only and cannot cross. ⛔ NOT keyed off _bare — NavPanel.js:222 writes chromeless = false every paint, so _bare is permanently FALSE on the panel. Nothing writes the view-mode axis on the panel instance, the way nothing writes pixelType on the DOM one.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The prism carries a screen-bounds guard, so a marker that cannot put ink on the glass costs nothing — which is what keeps the map honest once a design gives it a PANE narrower than the frame.

verifyVia.input: Render PRISM headlessly at the default 1.5 pc zoom and at the 10.34 pc ceiling, counting per-marker work and faded labels. No such test exists today — _renderLocal's per-marker loop has NO regression coverage at realistic density.
verifyVia.observable:
A marker whose dashed line cannot cross the drawable rect does no drawing, no hover test and no _labelQueue push.

⛔ THE PREDECESSOR HANDOFF'S §4.5 FIGURE DOES NOT REPRODUCE AND THIS AC IS RESCOPED ACCORDINGLY. It reported '143 markers projected, 120 (84%) off canvas at the default zoom'. Re-measured as a proper A/B — the real function against a () => true stub, same scene, 1560x860 — the saving is 0% at the default zoom, 0% at the 10.34 pc ceiling, 0% under rotation, 0% on a lateral pan, and 13% (31 of 237 arcs) on an R/F vertical pan. ⭐ The geometry explains it: the prism projects x = cx + dx * halfW * 0.92 where dx is normalised by the QUERY radius, so |dx| <= 1 and every queried star lands inside the frame. Only Y escapes, because it has its own window rather than the radius.

⭐⭐ SO THIS IS NOT A PERFORMANCE AC. It is a correctness guard that becomes load-bearing the day AC-4 lands: halfW equals the canvas only while the prism owns the whole canvas, and design 1 gives the map 43 of 71 columns beside the rail. The moment the pane is narrower than the frame the projection and the query decouple and nothing bounds |dx|. Verified by sabotage — unwiring the filter makes the probe read 250 against 250 and fail.
